answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate combined with the incumbent's price inflexibility and the low-cost vendor's qualifying quote creates a forcing decision within 14 days. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor executed onboarding quickly with accurate invoicing on prior work; memory_c4 shows renegotiation at renewal is only effective with a credible alternative. The incumbent has already refused to reopen—they will not move again. The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the mandate, eliminating the negotiation pathway. Assembly line is at 94% capacity with no buffer, making defer_decision risky (auto-renewal failure + emergency sourcing under pressure). Switching now with standard experiment rigor (staged volume increase, monitored quality/delivery metrics, 30-day confidence checkpoint) allows cost achievement while retaining ability to add second source (memory_c3 pattern) if primary supply falters. Risk: execution pressure in 14 days and dependency on single low-cost source initially; mitigated by proven onboarding speed and transition to dual-source once budget permits.
